lines.text: Short penultimate, so the plant became a stomp. Longer and lower next time.
Lengthen your penultimate. A longer, lower step lets the hips drop and load.
Your second-to-last step was choppy. Stretch it out so you can gather.
Think long penultimate, not late penultimate. That step is your gather.
Your penultimate overreached, so the brake became a slide. Keep it long, but controlled.
Brace your trunk on that long step, so you brake instead of sliding.
Reel that step in a touch. Long and controlled beats long and sliding.
Good penultimate. Long, low, and in control.
That second-to-last step set up the whole jump.
Long and low into the plant. That is your gather.
Nice. You lowered your hips with control on that step.
Pretty run, but you never loaded. Sink your hips into the gather.
You stayed tall. Sit into the gather so your legs can load.
Lower your hips a touch. No load, no spring.
You sank too deep and lost your bounce. Try a quicker, shallower gather.
Too much squat at that speed. Stay higher so the spring can fire.
Shorter dip next time. Lingering low turns your spring into heat, not height.
Your arms were late. Drive them down on the penultimate, then whip them up.
Arms down as the second-to-last step lands, then up through the takeoff. That adds lift.
Late swing, so the lift came after you left. Start the arms down sooner.
No arm swing. Swing both arms, that's twenty to thirty-eight percent more jump.
Your arms stayed quiet, and that's jump left on the floor. Swing both, hard.
Swing both arms back, then whip them up. Free height, every single jump.
Arms right on time. Down on the penultimate, up through takeoff.
Great arm timing. That swing added real height.
Down, then whip up. Your arms were working for you.
Beautiful swing. Arms and feet were in sync.
Your free knee stayed low. Drive it up for height and rhythm.
Drive that free knee toward your chest. It lifts the whole body.
Free leg, not a passenger. Drive that knee up for lift.
Free knee drove up. That's height and rhythm.
Nice knee drive. It pulled you right up.
Good. That free leg did its job.
Leaning at takeoff sends force out, not up. Stay tall over the plant.
Force has direction. Chest proud over the plant, and every bit goes up.
Get tall over the plant foot. Every degree of lean taxes your height.
You got up…
That jump measured…
Off the floor…
Your jump reads…
That's a new personal best!
New best. Your highest jump yet.
Personal record. The work is showing.
Highest you've ever gone. Remember that feeling.
A little under your usual. Check that long, low penultimate.
Down a little. Rest a moment; tired legs leak height.
Not your highest, and that's fine. Check your arm timing next rep.
A touch early. Wait for the top, where your hand is highest.
You swung before the peak. Let the jump rise, then finish.
Patience at the top. Finish early and you give away height.
A beat late, you were already falling. Finish right at the top.
Late finish, and the rim got away. Strike at the top.
Finish at the peak. On the way down, you've lost reach.
Right at the top. Perfect timing.
Finished at the peak. That's the window.
Great timing. You met the rim at your highest.
Top of the jump, ball through. Clean.
Throw your off arm down as the finishing hand rises. It lifts your reach.
Use the off arm. Drive it down and your finishing hand climbs higher.
Play the off arm with intent. Down low sends your finishing hand higher.
Stiff landing. Sit into your hips to spare your knees.
That landing was rigid. Let ankles, knees and hips share the load.
Bend your ankles when you land. They soak up the shock.
Knees caved in. Track them over your midfoot to protect the joint.
Land with knees over the middle of your feet. Knees stay safe.
Your knees drifted in. Keep them over the midfoot, so they last.
Good landing. Soft, organized, ready.
Nice landing. You could go again right away.
Landed on purpose. That's how you last.
Early release. Let your legs lift the ball, and release near the top.
Ride the jump a beat longer. The top gives you the cleanest release.
You shot on the way up. Let the jump lift the ball first.
Late release. Let go at the top while your legs still help.
Shooting on the way down costs you power. Release at the top.
You were already coming down. Let it go at the peak.
Released near the top. Right on time.
Good release point. The jump did the lifting.
On time. Legs up, ball out at the peak.
That's the timing. Top of the jump, soft release.
Low set point, easy to block. Set it at your forehead.
Raise your set point to the forehead. Higher is harder to block.
Ball sat at your chin. Set it higher, out of reach.
Your elbow flared out, so the ball went sideways. Tuck it under.
Elbow under the ball. It keeps the shot on a straight line.
Flared elbow. Line it up under the ball so it flies straight.
Hitch at the set point. One motion keeps your legs in it.
Two motions there. Flow through the set point so the power carries.
Don't park the ball up top. One smooth motion, legs to fingertips.
Hold that follow-through till the ball lands. It keeps the release clean.
Early drop on the follow-through. Hold it, let the wrist finish.
Hand came down early. Leave it up till the ball lands.
Hands back to your guard after every strike. That's your protection.
Low hands after the strike leave you open. Bring them right back.
Strike, then home. Hands up protects you for the next exchange.
All arm on that one. Turn your hips into it for power.
Power starts at the floor. Rotate your hips through the strike.
Turn the hips first, and the arm just delivers it.
Chin down, eyes up. A raised chin is exposed.
Your chin lifted. Tuck it so you stay protected.
Tuck that chin, eyes still up. Safer and sharper.
Clean strike. Hips in, hands home.
That's it. Power from the hips, guard right back.
Sharp. Everything turned together on that one.
Straight legs on that landing. Bend your knees to soak it up.
Let your knees be the suspension. Soft legs keep you riding.
You landed stiff. Knees absorb it so you ride away clean.
You stayed tall through that turn. Get low for balance.
Sink lower, weight over the board. That's where your balance lives.
Too upright in the turn. A lower stance grips the edge.
Low and balanced. Nice riding.
Great stance through that turn.
Smooth. Knees soft, weight centered.
Shake it off. Next one's yours.
That's how you learn. Go again.
No worries. Reset and breathe.
Good effort. Every rep teaches you something.
Stay with it. You're closer than you think.
That's the one. Everything lined up.
Beautiful rep, start to finish.
Clean from the approach to the landing.
Yes! That's the rep we're chasing.
Textbook. Remember exactly how that felt.
Drill time. Follow the targets and move with the rhythm.
Here comes a drill. Hit each target as it lights up.
Let's warm up. Watch the targets and match them.
Go.
Here we go.
Start now.
And go!
Nice.
Good rhythm.
That's it.
Clean.
Right on beat.
Pick it up.
Quicker now.
Faster feet.
Slow it down.
Easy, control it.
Smooth, not rushed.
Hold it there.
Stay right there.
Freeze. Hold steady.
In through the nose, slow out.
Breathe in deep, then let it out slow.
Nose in, and a long slow breath out.
Switch sides.
Other side now.
Now the other side.
Rest now. Shake it out.
Take a breather.
Good. Catch your breath.
Last one.
Final rep.
One more, finish strong.
Drill complete. Great work, that's timing and control in the bank.
And that's the drill. Nice job, your body is learning the rhythm.
Finished. Those clean reps are how a better athlete gets built.
Before we play, step back until your whole body is in the picture, with clear space around you and overhead.
Quick space check. Step back until I can see all of you, and clear the area around and above.
Step back.
A little farther back.
Back up a bit.
Come closer.
Step in a little.
Move in closer.
Move to your left.
A step to your left.
Move to your right.
A step to your right.
Your feet need to be in the picture.
I need to see your feet.
Reach both arms overhead so I can check the headroom.
Arms up high. Let's make sure nothing's above you.
Stand still for a moment.
Hold still, just a second.
All set. Raise both hands to start.
You're good to go. Hands up when ready.
Space looks great. Lift both hands and we begin.
